model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, retention on tangible common equity

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 consolidated net total income = interest earned 1,32,538.24 cr - interest expended 74,074.99 cr (NII 58,463.25 cr) + other income 29,673.71 cr = 88,136.96 cr. Source: Q4-FY2026 audited consolidated results, AXISBANK.NS_Quarterly_Q4-FY2026.txt:455-465. The Metrics.csv 'Revenue' column (1,622,119.5m) is gross total income (interest earned + other income) and is NOT the engine base; a bank's interest expense is its cost of goods.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-09-30: paid-up capital Rs 622.74 cr / Rs 2 face value = 311.37 cr shares issued (Q2-FY2027 results line 18) plus ~1.7 cr dilutive ESOP/ESU shares implied by the H1 FY27 basic-vs-diluted EPS gap (49.30 vs 49.03; FY25 annual report note 1.4 shows 1.84 cr dilutive shares from 18.4m options/units). Held FLAT: the ESOP fair-value cost is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count. No buybacks (Indian banks do not repurchase). Metrics.csv SharesOutstanding (3,128.2m at Q2 FY27) is the diluted weighted-average count the parser recorded, consistent with this figure.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deposits (Rs 14,50,288 cr) and borrowings (Rs 3,24,488 cr, incl. Tier-2/infrastructure bonds) at 30-Sep-2026 are a bank's operating funding, not net debt; their interest cost is already inside the net-total-income flow. Cash and RBI balances (Rs 1,33,722 cr) are CRR/liquidity assets, not surplus cash. Setting net_debt = 0 is the dcf-methods rule for deposit takers.
inputs.fcf_note: For a bank the 'FCF' anchors are earnings, not cash-flow-statement FCF (consolidated OCF was -Rs 8,637 cr in FY26 and +Rs 44,384 cr in FY25 purely on deposit/advance timing). reported_fcf = Group net profit 26,384.85 cr + ESOP expense 483.38 cr = 26,868.23 cr (pre-SBC earnings); last_fcf = Group net profit after minority interest and associate share, 26,384.85 cr = 263,848.5m (Q4-FY2026 results line 17). FCFE in each projected year is this earnings stream less the equity retained to fund balance-sheet growth (the 'capex' line).
inputs.sbc_source: Q4-FY2026 audited consolidated cash flow statement, 'Employee Stock Options Expense' Rs 483.38 crore (FY25 Rs 430.54 crore) at AXISBANK.NS_Quarterly_Q4-FY2026.txt:656; fair-value method for all grants after 31-Mar-2021 (FY25 annual report note 2.2). India has no cash tax on net-share settlement of ESOPs at the employer level, so no equity-award tax add-on.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single INR cost of equity 12.5% across all scenarios (risk charged once, via scenario weights), identical to the house India-bank precedents HDB and IBN so the three large private banks compare directly. Built in the flows' own currency: India 10-year G-sec ~6.5% + beta ~0.9-1.0 x India total equity risk premium ~6.0-6.5% = ~12.0-13.0%; matches the 12-13% CoE Indian brokers apply to large private banks. Axis's beta is modestly above HDFC/ICICI, but a per-ticker premium on top of probability-weighted scenarios would charge risk twice; the bear weight carries it instead.
inputs.lease_treatment: Indian GAAP for banks (RBI-prescribed Banking Regulation Act format): no Ind AS 116 / IFRS 16 right-of-use accounting; branch and office leases are operating rent inside operating expenses, already deducted before the pre-tax margin. Nothing is added to net debt. One treatment, consistently.
inputs.nci_treatment: Minority interest (Rs 163.06 cr FY26 share of profit) and the associate share of profit (Max Life Insurance, Rs 54.09 cr) are netted into the pre-tax margin at their pre-tax equivalents (/(1-0.25)) so that FY0 NOPAT ties to Group net profit of Rs 26,384.85 cr. No NCI deduction in the equity bridge (that would charge it twice). Minority balance Rs 1,241.26 cr at 30-Sep-2026.
inputs.tangible_equity_note: Tangible common equity at 31-Mar-2026 = shareholders' equity 2,15,035.35 cr (capital 621.63 + ESOP outstanding 1,456.43 + reserves 2,12,957.29) less goodwill on consolidation 289.24 cr, less goodwill embedded in the Max Life associate carrying value ~1,596.73 cr (FY25 annual, Schedule 8 note 2), less net deferred tax asset ~5,400 cr (FY25 consolidated DTA 4,615.16 cr + the 797.55 cr DTA recognised in Q4 FY26; RBI deducts DTA from CET1) = ~2,07,750 cr. TCE / FY26 net revenue = 2.357, rounded 2.36. The Citibank India consumer-business intangibles (Rs 8,714 cr) were written off through the P&L in Q4 FY23, so no acquisition intangibles remain on the balance sheet.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing table row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker' (residual income / FCFE at cost of equity). Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (HDB, IBN, USB, WFC, TFC, NTRS, NAB.AX); identical structure to HDB and IBN so the three India-bank valuations compare directly. Deposits are not net debt; OCF is meaningless for a bank. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = consolidated net total income (NII + other income; FY26 Rs 88,136.96 cr). 'ebitda' = profit before tax (after provisions, opex, depreciation) + ESOP expense + pre-tax-equivalent associate share - pre-tax-equivalent minority interest: FY26 32,293.47 + 483.38 + 72.1 - 217.4 = 32,631.5 cr = 37.03% of net revenue (reported); 40.7% excluding the Rs 3,232 cr of one-off standard-asset provisions (1,231 cr RBI-directed crop-loan reclassification in Q2 FY26 + 2,001 cr new standard-asset framework in Q4 FY26). FY0 check: (37.03 - 0.548)% x (1 - 0.1796) x 88,137 = 26,378 cr vs reported Group NP 26,384.85 cr. sbc_pct 0.55%. da_pct 0 (bank depreciation Rs 1,893 cr is an operating expense already inside PBT; branch/IT capex is maintenance funded within it). cash tax 25.0% forward: statutory 25.17% (22% + surcharge + cess), FY25 effective 23.4%, FY26 reported 17.96% only because of the Rs 2,193 cr one-off Citi-intangibles tax ruling (normalised 24.75%), H1 FY27 25.4%; cash taxes paid have run 21-22% of PBT on DTA timing, which reverses. 'capex' = equity retention required to grow the balance sheet at constant capital intensity = TCE/revenue x g/(1+g), in % of revenue: base 2.36 (holds CET1 near today's 14.61%, regulatory minimum 8.0% incl. CCB; Axis is not a D-SIB), bull 2.20 (ROE rising lets CET1 drift toward ~13.5% as excess capital is consumed by growth), bear 2.50 (RBI expected-credit-loss transition from FY28 and higher unsecured risk weights absorb capital). No excess CET1 is released to the bridge in base or bear. FY0 ROTE on year-end TCE = 26,385 / 2,07,750 = 12.7% (cons. ROE 13.1% on average equity; H1 FY27 annualised 14.23%). Growth is net-total-income growth, not loan growth: H1 FY27 +6.3% YoY, Q2 FY27 +8.9% YoY and +3.2% QoQ, with management calling Q1 FY27 the NIM trough (3.46% -> 3.36% in Q2 on FCNR(B) drag, 3.47% ex-FCNR) and advances +23% YoY (+19% ex FCNR(B)-backed loans). YEAR-1 (FY27) is the only year judged off current-year evidence; years 2-10 are medium-term paths. band_position is not meaningful: ESOP cost is 0.55% of net revenue so the house/street band is a few rupees wide. Price is NSE INR, statements are INR: no currency bridge. Valuation date is seven months into FY27; FY27 is discounted one full period per house convention.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (net total income FY23 Rs 62,766 cr -> FY26 Rs 88,137 cr), cross-checked against equity 5yr CAGR 15.7%; used as the medium-term (years 2-4) base growth, with FY27 judged lower at 8.5% off the H1 run-rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS and earnings CAGRs (28-35%) exceed the equity CAGR (15.7-18.3%) by far more than 30% because the base years are troughs: FY21 was COVID-provision-depressed and FY23 carried the Rs 12,490 cr Citi acquisition write-off. Neither earnings CAGR is a forward growth rate; net-revenue and equity CAGRs are the usable ones.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs are on net total income (NII + other income), the engine base, not on the gross 'Revenue' column of Metrics.csv. FCF CAGRs are on the FCFE proxy Group net profit less ESOP expense (FY21 71,955m with ESOP at intrinsic value ~0; FY23 105,324m; FY26 259,015m). Equity CAGR is on consolidated shareholders' funds (FY21 1,035,937m; FY23 1,297,817m; FY26 2,150,354m). SBC is 0.4-0.6% of net revenue throughout, so the owner and reported series are essentially identical; SBC is not eating the growth.

base.growth_rationale: FY27 8.5%: H1 net revenue +6.3% YoY, Q2 +8.9% with NIM off the Q1 trough and advances +19-23%; H2 accelerates. FY28-FY30 12-13%: loan growth ~300bps above system (~14-15%) partly offset by FCNR(B) unwind and a gradual NIM recovery toward management's ~3.8% through-cycle target over 15-18 months. Fades to 7% by year 10 toward 6.5% terminal (Indian nominal GDP ~10% today, long-run bank growth below it).
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin on net revenue (PBT + ESOP - NCI). FY24 ~45.7%, FY25 43.8%, FY26 37.0% reported / 40.7% ex one-off provisions, H1 FY27 44.5% on a 0.45% net credit cost that is below the 15-year average. 43% in FY27 (H1 44.5%, H2 credit cost normalising) then 42.5% flat: NIM recovery and falling cost-to-assets (2.14%, down 24bps YoY) offset by credit cost normalising to ~0.7-0.8% and the RBI ECL transition from FY28.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 236 x g/(1+g) percent of net revenue (TCE/revenue 2.36 held constant, CET1 held near 14.6%). Implied FCFE payout is near zero in the 13%-growth years and ~50% of earnings by year 10, which is the arithmetic of a bank growing close to its ~13% ROTE; the Rs 1/share dividend (4% payout) is what Axis actually distributes today.

bull.growth_rationale: NIM back at 3.7-3.8% within 18 months as FCNR(B) deposits run off and loan repricing completes; SBB/SME/mid-corporate keep compounding 20%+; Citi affluent franchise and subsidiaries (Axis Finance PAT +42%, Axis Capital +61%) add fee growth.
bull.margin_rationale: Credit cost stays 0.5-0.6% on a granular book (management: new credit costs structurally below the FY12-26 average), cost-to-assets falls below 2%, NIM 3.8%: pre-tax margin reaches FY24's 45.7% and a little beyond. Implied ROTE ~15.5%.
bull.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 220 x g/(1+g) percent of net revenue (TCE/revenue 2.20: part of today's ~6pp CET1 headroom over the 8.0% minimum is consumed by growth rather than held).

bear.growth_rationale: NIM stuck at 3.3-3.4%: deposit competition and the FCNR(B) unwind keep funding costs high while EBLR-linked loans reprice down; CASA keeps sliding from 35%; growth converges on system credit growth of ~10% rather than 300bps above it.
bear.margin_rationale: An unsecured-retail and SME credit cycle in FY28-FY29 (credit cost 1.4-1.5%, as in FY20-21) plus the RBI ECL transition and further supervisory provisions of the Q2 FY26 kind; margin recovers only to 38% (credit cost ~1.0%, NIM 3.4%). Implied ROTE ~11%.
bear.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 250 x g/(1+g) percent of net revenue (TCE/revenue 2.50: higher unsecured risk weights and ECL provisioning absorb capital, so more equity is retained per rupee of revenue).

scenario_narratives.base: Axis stays India's third/fourth private bank, growing net revenue ~12-13% a year through FY30 as loans compound ~300bps above system and NIM climbs back from the Q1 FY27 trough (3.46%, 3.36% in Q2 on FCNR(B) drag) toward but not fully to the ~3.8% through-cycle target. Credit cost normalises from H1 FY27's cyclically low 0.45% to ~0.7-0.8%, cost-to-assets keeps falling, and the RBI expected-credit-loss transition from FY28 is absorbed without a capital raise. Pre-tax margin on net revenue settles at 42.5%, ROTE ~13%, CET1 held near 14.6% by retaining almost all earnings while growth runs at 12-13%. Value is the FCFE this leaves after retention, capitalised at a 12.5% INR cost of equity with 6.5% terminal growth; the terminal value is Gordon-bound just under the 18x FCFE cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: The FCNR(B) deposits run off and the loan book finishes repricing, taking NIM to 3.7-3.8% inside management's 15-18 month window; SBB, SME and mid-corporate (24% of loans) keep growing 20%+; the Citi affluent and Burgundy franchises and the subsidiaries (Axis Finance, Capital, AMC, Securities, PAT growth 9-61%) lift fee income. Credit cost holds 0.5-0.6% on a more granular book, cost-to-assets falls below 2%, and pre-tax margin reaches 46%, ROTE ~15.5%. Growth of 14-15% in FY28-FY30 is funded partly by consuming CET1 headroom (TCE/revenue 2.20 rather than 2.36), so more of the earnings reach shareholders.
scenario_narratives.bear: Deposit competition and the FCNR(B) unwind keep funding costs high while EBLR loans reprice down, so NIM is stuck at 3.3-3.4% and CASA keeps sliding from 35%. Unsecured retail (cards, personal loans; Axis is more exposed than HDFC/ICICI) and SME/agri slip into a credit cycle in FY28-FY29 with credit cost at 1.4-1.5%, the RBI's ECL framework and further supervisory provisions of the Q2 FY26 crop-loan kind add to it, and growth converges on system credit growth. Pre-tax margin troughs at 36% and recovers only to 38% (ROTE ~11%); higher risk weights mean more capital is retained per rupee of revenue (TCE/revenue 2.50). Slower growth frees some capital, which is why the bear value is not proportionally lower than the earnings hit.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% and bull cut from 35% to 25%, matching the HDB precedent: the NIM recovery to 3.8% has no dated guidance and has lagged peers, FY26 carried an RBI-directed one-time provision that shows live supervisory risk, Axis is the most unsecured-retail-exposed of the large private banks, and the FY28 ECL transition is an unquantified capital call. The bull case needs NIM, credit cost and cost-to-assets to all move the right way together, which argues against overweighting it; operating momentum (PAT +38% YoY in Q2 FY27, GNPA 1.16%, CET1 14.6%) keeps it at a full 25%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on the equity cash flow left after it has retained the capital its growth requires, discounted at the cost of equity in the currency of its flows. Axis earns a ~13% ROTE and wants to grow 12-13%, so for the next several years it must retain nearly all of its earnings; shareholders are paid in book-value growth, not cash, and the value today rests on the payout that becomes possible once growth slows toward 7%. At a 12.5% INR cost of equity that stream is worth materially less than the market pays; the required-return table shows the price discounts something nearer a 9% rupee cost of equity on the base path, or the bull path, which is the same read the house reached on HDB and IBN.
key_risks_to_valuation: NIM: every 10bps of sustained NIM on ~Rs 20trn of interest-earning assets is ~Rs 2,000 cr of pre-tax profit, ~2pp of margin; the 3.8% through-cycle target vs 3.36% today is the single largest swing factor and has no dated guidance.
Credit cost: H1 FY27's 0.45% is below the 15-year average; the base assumes ~0.7-0.8%, the bear a 1.4-1.5% cycle in unsecured retail/SME.

RBI expected-credit-loss transition (from FY28, glide path) and standard-asset provisioning changes: one-time provisions of Rs 3,232 cr hit FY26; a larger ECL day-one charge would reduce both earnings and CET1.
FCNR(B) deposits of Rs 1,018 bn raised under the RBI special window inflate reported deposit and loan growth; their run-off will show in FY27-FY28 growth optics and funding cost.

Capital intensity assumption: the model holds TCE/net revenue constant (CET1 ~14.6%). If Axis chose to run CET1 down toward 12-13%, FCFE would be higher for several years (partly captured in the bull case).
Cost of equity: the valuation is linear in the 12.5% INR CoE assumption; Indian domestic flows price large private banks at an implied 9-11%, which is the gap between this model and the market.

Tangible-equity estimate: the Mar-26 DTA (~Rs 5,400 cr) is estimated from the FY25 consolidated figure plus the Q4 FY26 recognition; a Rs 1,000 cr error moves TCE/revenue by 0.01 and value by well under 1%.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (NSE: AXISBANK) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1150.3-1418.3; INR, same currency as the statements, so no FX bridge.
data_sources.financials: Q4-FY2026 audited consolidated results and cash flow (year to 31-Mar-2026); Q2-FY2027 unaudited consolidated results and balance sheet (30-Sep-2026); FY2025 Integrated Annual Report (EPS dilution note 1.4, ESOP note 2.2, DTA note 2.8/1.11, goodwill in associate); Q2-FY2027 investor presentation (NIM, CET1 walk, credit-cost history, ROE). All Indian GAAP, Rs crore converted to Rs millions (x10).
data_sources.qualitative: AXISBANK.NS_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): guidance block (NIM ~3.8% through-cycle over 15-18 months, loan growth ~300bps above system, credit-cost guidance withheld for FY27, CET1 ~14.6%), recent developments, bull/bear cases.
